items.a: PICLAB is an independent educational website for learning PIC18 architecture, reading pin/register references, studying embedded-C concepts, and following experiment manuals.

items.q: Does PICLAB include a circuit builder or interactive lab simulator?
items.a: No. The standalone Circuit Lab and experiment simulation controls were intentionally removed. Experiment pages provide manual-style instructions, connection guidance, source-code listings where supplied, code explanations and viva questions.

PICLAB is dedicated to the PIC18F4520. Its pinout is mapped for the 40-pin DIP package, and the register explorer contains a curated educational subset. Verify details against the official PIC18F4520 datasheet before hardware work.

In the classic PIC18 GPIO model, a TRIS bit of 1 configures the corresponding GPIO as an input; a 0 configures it as an output. Analog configuration and peripheral multiplexing may further affect pin behaviour.
LAT registers represent output latches. Writing LAT and reading PORT are different operations; peripheral multiplexing can also affect which function controls a pin.
Progress, the selected device and preferences are stored in this browser using LocalStorage. Use Settings to export or import a JSON backup. Data does not sync between devices.

items.q: Is the Login ID a real account?
items.a: No. It is a local profile label only. PICLAB has no backend authentication, account recovery or multi-device sync. Do not enter passwords or sensitive personal information.
No. PICLAB is an independent educational project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Microchip Technology. Verify device facts using the official datasheet before real hardware work.

items.q: Can I upload example code directly to hardware?
items.a: Treat examples as teaching material. Confirm device, clock, configuration bits, pin multiplexing, current limits, driver circuitry and compiler version before programming a physical board.
